subject: Post-call recap: logging export, immutability, and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap: logging export, immutability, and next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning — good conversation. Per our discovery call, I wanted to summarize what we covered on audit logging and confirm next steps so your security team can triage. TL;DR: Redwood provides comprehensive admin + API logs, supports export delivery, and offers configurable retention/immutability controls; Karthik will follow up with tech specifics for your S3 delivery and immutability options.

What we covered (high level):
- SOC 2 status: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (summary attached). Full report available under NDA.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing addenda and can enable HIPAA agreements for covered customers.
- Admin activity logs: capture sign-ins, role changes, permission grants, console actions with actor, timestamp, IP, and request context.
- API request/response logs: per-request metadata and error traces; payload redaction by default for PII.
- Exportability: logs can be exported on-demand as ndjson, daily batched S3 delivery, or streamed via secure API.
- Immutability: we offer write-once retention windows and signed manifests for delivered batches to support tamper-evidence.

Requested follow-ups / action items:
1) CardiaSys: send over your vendor security questionnaire and specific retention/immutability policy language to confirm fit (Lara?)
2) Redwood: Karthik to send an S3 delivery & signing options doc + example ndjson schema (attached: redwood-audit-log-spec.pdf)
3) Redwood: provide SOC 2 artifacts under NDA if you want the full report (attached: SOC2-TypeII-summary-2025.pdf)
4) Align on a short POA for onboarding (we typically do a security intake -> test export -> S3 acceptance -> production switch)

Next meeting: propose 06/17, 10:00 PT for the technical handoff — happy to adjust.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging export, immutability, and next steps

Thanks, Andrew — great questions. Looping in Karthik and Vivek to own the technical answers. Quick notes while they jump in:
- CMK/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS for S3 delivery; can support rotating CMKs and HSM-backed keys via our key-integration path.
- Retention: retention is configurable by log class (admin / api / audit) and we can set retention windows and legal-hold flags on export buckets.
- Signed manifests: this is our standard delivery integrity artifact — each daily batch includes a JSON manifest with SHA256 checksums for each file plus a signature signed by Redwood's signing key. We can optionally publish a timestamped signature (RFC 3161 style) or sign with a customer-validated key for extra proof chain.

Karthik / Vivek: can you confirm the S3 object lock compatibility and the exact manifest format (schema + example) so we can send to CardiaSys before 06/17? Also please indicate whether we can deliver a pre-signed object-list within the manifest that CardiaSys can cross-check using their own KMS.

Olga
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@cardiasys.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@cardiasys.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging export, immutability, and next steps

Hi Andrew / Lara — Karthik here. Brief technical answers and an attachment with examples (redwood-audit-log-spec.pdf). Copied the key points below: 

1) Manifest & immutability compatibility:
- Manifest format: ndjson list where first record is metadata (batch_id, timestamp_utc, signed_by, signature_alg) followed by file entries: {"path":"...","sha256":"...","size_bytes":12345,"log_type":"admin"}. Example manifests included in the spec.
- We can sign manifests using an RSA/ECDSA key pair that Redwood holds. If you prefer, we can accept your public key and sign the manifest with a customer-bound signature (we can also include your signature field so you can run independent verification).
- S3 Object Lock: we are compatible. We can write to your pre-provisioned bucket with Object Lock enabled; our delivery agent will set retention mode GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE as requested. For COMPLIANCE-mode write-once, the bucket must be under your account and Object Lock enabled at bucket creation.

2) KMS & encryption:
- S3 delivery supports SSE-S3, SSE-KMS (customer CMK), and client-side encryption. For CMK, the delivered objects will be encrypted with your CMK in your AWS account; Redwood will not retain the unencrypted object. We support key rotation and will work with your KMS policy to ensure delivery IAM roles are permitted.

3) Retention windows & log classes:
- Configurable per-log-type. Example: admin logs (7y), api request logs (2y), analytics logs (90d). You can request custom retention per log_type at onboarding and we implement as bucket lifecycle + legal hold alignments.

4) Roadmap / sandbox plan for 06/17 call:
- Pre-call: we will provision a test delivery to your staging S3 (you provide bucket ARN + KMS key ARN), ship a 48-hour sample with manifest, and you validate checksums & Object Lock behavior.
- On call: handoff to infra/security to validate policy, handshake on KMS roles, and sign off on retention/immunity requirements.

Deliverables before call (eta 06/15):
- Example manifest + ndjson schema (in the attached spec)
- Step-by-step S3 provisioning guide for your infra team
- Completed sections of your vendor questionnaire (we'll fill security controls and encryption sections by 06/14)

If you want, we can run an accelerated POC and bring our SRE on the 06/17 call.

-Karthik
